title: Nvidia-backed Upscale AI launches platform to connect chips from rival suppliers
key_facts: Upscale AI, a Santa Clara networking startup backed by Nvidia, launched Token Fabric on Thursday 8 Oct.
It works with GPUs, custom AI chips and network cards from any vendor, using open standards including UALink and ESUN.
It combines Upscale's SkyFabriX scale-up switch chip with scale-out switches built on Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet chips.
Software layers SkyOS and SkyCMD run and monitor the network and can flag bottlenecks and hardware that may need replacement.
First part due in Q4; rest rolling out through 2027; the company statement puts general availability in early 2027.
CEO Barun Kar expects Token Fabric revenue in the tens of millions of dollars next year, possibly the low hundreds of millions.
quote_evidence: Upscale AI, a Santa Clara networking startup backed by Nvidia, launched a platform on Thursday that lets data centres link AI chips made by different suppliers, Reuters reported.
Chief executive Barun Kar told Reuters he expects Token Fabric revenue next year in the tens of millions of dollars, possibly reaching the low hundreds of millions.
Token Fabric combines SkyFabriX, Upscale’s own scale-up switch chip, with scale-out switches built on Nvidia’s Spectrum-X Ethernet chips.
why_it_matters_hint: Open-standard network for mixed-vendor AI chips; early stage.
